source.title: Conditional Importance in Toy Models of Superposition

record.file_problem: The post is present, but some equations and visualized Gram-matrix results are missing or blank in the supplied web text. The text describes several results without the underlying plots or their numerical values.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports toy-model experiments and argues that conditional importance alone does not make superposition easier, distinguishing it from anti-correlated feature values.
record.gate_note: The post compares conditional importance, fixed importance, and an anti-correlated-features setup. It reports qualitative Gram-matrix findings and approximate counts in text. The sparsity probability and some equations are not recoverable from the supplied text. The three training phases are described, but phase-specific geometry results are not separately available.
record.test_reason: A new toy-model setting (datapoint-dependent conditional importance) that reports its own Gram-matrix results on how features are superposed. These results show features stored in fewer dimensions, interference, importance-prioritised allocation and anti-correlated sharing. The post argues against an intuition about conditional importance, not against any claim version, so T3 fits better than T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Features not being important at the same time does not make them easier to superpose; feature values must be anti-correlated. Re-encoding conditional importance as anti-correlated features allows more superposition, if the model can infer the context.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the toy-model projection-and-reconstruction setup, but investigates datapoint-dependent conditional importance and compares it with fixed importance and an anti-correlated-feature setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported geometry is qualitatively similar for conditional and fixed importance; the anti-correlated-feature setup instead represents all 20 features with no within-subset interference.

fits_no_version.finding: Conditional importance (importance anti-correlated, feature values independent) yields the same superposition pattern as fixed importance. Only anti-correlation of feature values enables extra sharing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Superposition geometry depends on correlation of feature values, not on context-dependent importance alone.

record.problems: The supplied text omits equations and the plots on which the Gram-matrix descriptions depend. The sparsity probability is not recoverable, results are qualitative, and no per-seed values or statistical uncertainty are reported.
record.rows_left_out: The post mentions visualizations at random initialization, 4 epochs, and 12 epochs, but does not provide phase-specific geometry outcomes or numeric values in the supplied text, so these are not separate rows.

untested.parts: No sparsity sweep or phase transition; the sparsity value is unrecoverable. No quantified near-orthogonality and no regular polytope geometry.
No neurons or privileged basis are examined, so neuron polysemanticity is not measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 limits_scope label is dropped. V1 makes no claim about conditional importance, so the null effect of conditional importance is recorded under fits_no_version instead. All results are qualitative, from a blog post with 3 seeds per setup and no uncertainty; the plots and sparsity value are absent from the text.

versions.untested_parts: No sparsity sweep or transition is reported; the sparsity probability is missing from the supplied text. The results do not quantify how nearly orthogonal the directions are or establish regular geometry across settings.
The study is a toy-model feature-reconstruction experiment, not a test of polysemantic neurons in language models. It does not directly measure dedicated neuron assignments.
No alternative, non-capacity mechanism for polysemantic neurons is tested.
No LLM activations, neuron-level feature spread, or SAE recovery is studied.
No SAE features or claims about their completeness, stability, or canonical status are evaluated.
The study does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.
